criticalCorrections: The current DOXA timeline names the 1967 debut SUB 300. The article distinguishes the later 300T family and current descendants instead of backdating today's SUB 300T to 1967.
DOXA history and Eschle's firsthand retrospective interview name Lake Neuchatel. Lake Geneva and laboratory test pools were not verified and are not described as facts.
Thirty metres is attributed to Eschle's reported trials, not presented as a universal optimum or a depth where orange remains unchanged in every body of water.
Claude Wesly worked with the team and connected Eschle to US Divers. Cousteau personally performing the lake colour trials was not established.
Patent US3505808A states Swiss priority 1967-04-14, US filing 1968-04-10 and grant 1970-04-14. Manufacturer blog's conflated dates are not repeated.
Conquistador chronology conflicts between current DOXA material (1968) and Eschle interview (1969). A precise debut year and helium-valve priority are not asserted.

The 1966 debut in Eschle's retrospective interview and 1967 SUB 300T naming in the MIH release differ from the current manufacturer's 1967 SUB 300 timeline. These discrepancies remain explicitly documented in private comments.
Historical bezel direction is not generalised from modern specifications. The MIH release calls its archival bezel bidirectional; the article explicitly attributes unidirectionality to today's watch.

Modern references 821.10.351.10 and 840.10.351.10 describe current steel-bracelet Professional models, not historical 1967 examples. ETA 2872 is restricted to the later French naval variant reported by DOXA. Modern movement supplier is not guessed.
Museum number 5042 identifies the specific 1970 naval watch, not a retail model reference.
